findings.finding: An S-8 registering 5,087,548 Class A shares under the 2026 Stock Incentive Plan became effective when filed on 2026-09-11, and an F-3 for a $200M mixed shelf was declared effective on 2026-09-10. Together they give the issuer an open issuance channel that can put shares into the 2026-09-30 session.
findings.mechanism_in_window: An S-8 is effective the day it is filed and needs no further filing before shares are granted and resold. The shelf is also effective. So supply can reach the tape on 2026-09-30 without any new document; this is the same logic as an open ATM, not a later-dated event. The issuer has a record of cheap supply: best-efforts units at $0.79 in July 2026, with zero-exercise-price warrants worth 2 shares each (16M shares), and a $0.40 insider placement agreed on 2026-09-07. It has no prior S-8 usage on EDGAR.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: This stock fell from $8.58 (2026-09-17) to $2.04 over eight sessions, mostly on thin volume. That is consistent with continuous supply, but no filing ties any of it to the S-8. The July unit offering was followed by a run-up and then the -89.65% fall on 2026-09-03 (baseline history).
findings.why_not_priced: 5,087,548 was about 20% of the 25.4M pre-split shares, and about 203k post-split if the plan is adjusted, against 1,017,510 Class A shares outstanding. The price holds the fall but not a known draw rate. If the market were pricing a completed draw, the fall would sit on heavy volume. Instead it came on 0.69x, so the supply may still be arriving rather than spent.
findings.independence: The $200M F-3 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/2018529/000121390026089705/ea0296968-f3_intercont.htm), declared effective 2026-09-10, is a second channel that is live on the same terms. It is independent of the S-8 as a document, though not as a behaviour.

outside_window.finding: The CEO's 1,625,000 Class B shares at $0.40 were not split-adjusted (the subscription agreement has no adjustment clause, and the Form 4 shows a 1,831,598.04 holding). The 424B4 describes Class B as convertible to Class A at the holder's option. This is a large economic overhang against about 1.02M Class A shares at $2. It is known since 2026-09-11 and 2026-09-25, and no conversion is dated.

A second reverse split inside one year: 25-for-1 in April 2026 and again on 2026-09-17, a cumulative 625x. Under Nasdaq's rules there is no cure period if the stock falls back below $1. At $2.04 that is not near within one session.
The 20-F for the fiscal year to June 30, 2026 is due by 2026-10-31.

Up to 16M Class A shares (pre-split) were issuable at zero price under the July 2026 warrants, which expire around January 2027. Their remaining balance is unknown and is probably largely exercised already, given the August run-up and the September collapse.
